chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayoub, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Religion will not cease to be standing as long as the Ka'bah stands.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Ka'ah in relation to the permanence of Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith links the continuity of the divine religion (al-Din) to the physical presence of the Ka'bah, serving as a tangible sign of monotheistic worship. Scholars interpret this as indicating that the Ka'bah is not merely a structure but a enduring symbol of the covenant between God and humanity, ensuring the persistence of Islamic practice and identity throughout history.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Abu Al Magra, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Religion would not cease to be standing for as long as the Kabah is standing’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from abu al- Mighra’ from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
religion (al-Islam) will continue to exist as long as al-Ka‘bah is maintained.”
